lessons.title: Lit materials render black without a light or an environment
lessons.symptom: The mesh is there (it hides the background) but it is pure black.
lessons.cause: MeshStandardMaterial, MeshPhysicalMaterial, MeshLambertMaterial and MeshPhongMaterial only reflect light. With no light and no scene.environment there is nothing to reflect.
lessons.fix: Add a HemisphereLight plus a DirectionalLight, or set scene.environment from a RoomEnvironment through PMREMGenerator. Use MeshBasicMaterial only for things that should ignore light.
lessons.test: Swap the material for MeshNormalMaterial: if the shape shows, the scene is fine and only light is missing.

lessons.title: A camera left at the origin sits inside the model and sees nothing
lessons.symptom: Blank canvas, or only the background, even though the scene has a mesh at the origin.
lessons.cause: Cameras start at position 0, 0, 0 looking down negative Z. A mesh at the origin then surrounds the camera, and its faces point away from it, so they are culled.
lessons.fix: Move the camera back (camera.position.set(0, 1, 5)) and call camera.lookAt(0, 0, 0), or frame the model with its Box3 size.
lessons.test: Log camera.position and the model's Box3; the camera should be outside the box, at a distance of about twice its size.

lessons.title: A container without a height gives a canvas of 0 pixels
lessons.symptom: Nothing shows and no error is printed; the canvas element exists but has a height of 0, or a fixed 300 by 150.
lessons.cause: renderer.setSize(container.clientWidth, container.clientHeight) ran while the container had no CSS height (a div grows only with its content), or before it was laid out.
lessons.fix: Give html, body and the container a height (100% or 100vh), size the renderer from the container in a ResizeObserver, and call setSize again when it changes. The R3F Canvas fills its parent the same way, so that parent needs a height too.
lessons.test: In the browser console, read renderer.domElement.width and height: both must be above 0.

lessons.title: The renderer draws into a canvas that is never put on the page
lessons.symptom: No error, no picture: the page shows only its HTML.
lessons.cause: WebGLRenderer creates its own canvas element. Unless renderer.domElement is appended to the document, or an existing canvas is passed in the options, it stays off screen.
lessons.fix: Append renderer.domElement to the container, or pass the canvas of the page as the canvas option.

lessons.title: Rendering once before an async load leaves the old frame on screen
lessons.symptom: The model or texture loads (the network tab shows it) but never appears until the window is resized.
lessons.cause: The code renders one frame right away and has no animation loop. Loaders finish later, and nothing draws a frame after that.
lessons.fix: Use renderer.setAnimationLoop, or render again in the load callback and on every control change when you render on demand.

lessons.title: renderer.render takes the scene first and the camera second
lessons.symptom: Nothing is drawn and the console says the camera is not an instance of THREE.Camera.
lessons.cause: The arguments were swapped: renderer.render(camera, scene).
lessons.fix: Call renderer.render(scene, camera).
errors: camera is not an instance of THREE.Camera

lessons.title: A near plane of 0 breaks the depth buffer
lessons.symptom: Flickering surfaces, objects showing through each other, or nothing at all.
lessons.cause: Depth precision depends on the ratio of far to near. With near at 0 the ratio is infinite and every depth collapses to the same value.
lessons.fix: Use near 0.1 (or as large as the scene allows) and a far that just fits the scene. Big worlds can turn on logarithmicDepthBuffer in the renderer options.

lessons.title: Two faces at the same depth flicker against each other
lessons.symptom: Stripes or moving patterns where a decal, a road or a floor lies on another surface, worse when the camera moves away.
lessons.cause: Both faces write nearly the same depth, so rounding decides which one wins per pixel. A far plane much larger than the scene makes it worse.
lessons.fix: Lift the top surface a little, or set polygonOffset with polygonOffsetFactor -1 on its material. Bring far down to what the scene needs, and raise near.

lessons.title: After a resize the picture is stretched until the projection is updated
lessons.symptom: Circles look like ovals, or the scene looks squashed after the window or the panel changes size.
lessons.cause: camera.aspect changed but the projection matrix was not rebuilt, or nothing listens for the resize at all.
lessons.fix: On resize: set camera.aspect, call camera.updateProjectionMatrix() and renderer.setSize() with the new size. Use a ResizeObserver on the container when the canvas is not full screen.

lessons.title: Every new renderer takes a WebGL context, and the browser drops the oldest
lessons.symptom: After a few route changes or hot reloads the canvas goes black, and the console shows a lost context.
lessons.cause: Browsers allow only a handful of WebGL contexts per page (about 16 in Chrome). Creating a renderer per component or per reload and never releasing it uses them up. A GPU reset loses the context too.
lessons.fix: Keep one renderer for the page. When a view unmounts, call renderer.setAnimationLoop(null), renderer.dispose() and renderer.forceContextLoss(). Handle webglcontextlost with event.preventDefault() if the page should recover.

lessons.title: WebGL 2 must be available: WebGLRenderer dropped WebGL 1 in r163
lessons.symptom: The renderer throws while being created, on an old device, in a VM, or when hardware acceleration is off.
lessons.cause: The browser cannot give a WebGL 2 context: no GPU driver, the GPU is blocklisted, or the context attributes asked for are not supported. Since r163 WebGLRenderer does not fall back to WebGL 1.
lessons.fix: Catch the error and show a message instead of a blank page. Ask the user to turn on hardware acceleration; for headless tests start Chromium with SwiftShader (threesmith check does this).
errors: A WebGL context could not be created

lessons.title: Transparent objects hide each other in the wrong order
lessons.symptom: Glass, particles or a see-through mesh makes the objects behind it vanish, or the order pops as the camera turns.
lessons.cause: Transparent objects are sorted per object by distance, not per pixel, and by default they still write depth, so whatever draws first blocks what is behind it.
lessons.fix: Set depthWrite false on transparent materials, give fixed layers a renderOrder, and split big transparent meshes into parts that sort well.

lessons.title: Use alphaTest, not transparent, for leaves, fences and hair cards
lessons.symptom: Leaves or a fence texture show dark or white boxes around the shapes, or parts of the tree vanish behind other leaves.
lessons.cause: A cutout texture drawn as transparent blends and sorts badly; the clear parts of the texture still write depth.
lessons.fix: Set alphaTest to 0.5 and leave transparent false. For softer edges with MSAA, use alphaToCoverage.

lessons.title: A plane is visible from one side only, and PlaneGeometry stands upright
lessons.symptom: The floor is missing, or it shows from below but not from above, or it stands like a wall.
lessons.cause: PlaneGeometry lies in the XY plane facing +Z, and materials draw only front faces.
lessons.fix: For a floor, rotate it with rotation.x set to -Math.PI / 2. Use side DoubleSide only when both sides must show.

lessons.title: linewidth has no effect on lines with WebGL
lessons.symptom: Lines stay 1 pixel wide whatever linewidth is set to.
lessons.cause: WebGL implementations draw lines at 1 pixel; LineBasicMaterial cannot change that.
lessons.fix: Use Line2 with LineGeometry and LineMaterial from three/addons/lines/ for wide lines, or build thin meshes (tubes or ribbons).

lessons.title: Do not sample a render target while rendering into it
lessons.symptom: A mirror, a portal or a post effect goes black, and the console fills with feedback loop warnings.
lessons.cause: A mesh in the scene uses the render target's texture while that same target is being drawn.
lessons.fix: Hide the mesh that shows the texture while you render into the target, or use two render targets and swap them each frame.
errors: Feedback loop formed between Framebuffer and active Texture

lessons.title: Color textures need colorSpace set to SRGBColorSpace
lessons.symptom: Textures look washed out and pale, or darker and more saturated than the image file.
lessons.cause: TextureLoader gives textures NoColorSpace, so three treats the sRGB pixels of a photo or a painted map as linear values. GLTFLoader sets it for you; your own TextureLoader code does not.
lessons.fix: Set texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace on map, emissiveMap and other color maps, and on CanvasTexture and VideoTexture that show color.
lessons.test: Show the texture on a MeshBasicMaterial plane next to the image in an img tag: the colors must match.

lessons.title: Normal, roughness, metalness and AO maps stay linear
lessons.symptom: Lighting on a textured model looks wrong: bumps point the wrong way, surfaces are too shiny or too rough.
lessons.cause: Data maps hold numbers, not colors. Marking them SRGBColorSpace makes three convert them, which changes the values.
lessons.fix: Leave normalMap, roughnessMap, metalnessMap, aoMap, displacementMap and alphaMap at NoColorSpace; only color maps get SRGBColorSpace.

lessons.title: outputEncoding and texture encoding were replaced by color spaces in r152
lessons.symptom: Code from an old tutorial sets renderer.outputEncoding or texture.encoding, which does nothing now, and the import of sRGBEncoding fails.
lessons.cause: r152 replaced outputEncoding with outputColorSpace and Texture.encoding with Texture.colorSpace, and turned ColorManagement on by default.
lessons.fix: Delete renderer.outputEncoding (sRGB output is the default) and replace texture.encoding with texture.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace.

lessons.title: Leave ColorManagement on so hex colors match the design
lessons.symptom: Material colors set from hex values look different from the same colors in CSS, and lighting looks harsh.
lessons.cause: With ColorManagement turned off, three treats hex colors as linear values and skips the sRGB conversion, so colors and light falloff are wrong.
lessons.fix: Remove ColorManagement.enabled = false. Write colors as hex or CSS strings; three converts them from sRGB.

lessons.title: Tone mapping changes flat colors, so UI and brand colors look dull
lessons.symptom: A logo, a flat colored panel or a pure white looks greyish or shifted in hue.
lessons.cause: ACESFilmicToneMapping and AgXToneMapping compress bright values and shift hues. That suits lit scenes, not colors that must be exact.
lessons.fix: Set toneMapped false on materials that must keep their color, or use NeutralToneMapping, or NoToneMapping when nothing is lit.

lessons.title: With EffectComposer, OutputPass does the color space and tone mapping, once
lessons.symptom: With post processing the scene is too dark, or too bright and washed out.
lessons.cause: The composer renders into linear render targets, so the conversion to sRGB and tone mapping have to happen in a final pass. Old code adds a gamma correction pass as well, which converts twice.
lessons.fix: Add OutputPass from three/addons/postprocessing/OutputPass.js as the last pass and remove any gamma correction pass.

lessons.title: Set a material color with color.set(), not by assigning a number
lessons.symptom: Changing a color at runtime does nothing or throws.
lessons.cause: material.color is a Color object. Assigning 0xff0000 to it replaces the object with a number that the renderer cannot read.
lessons.fix: Call material.color.set(0xff0000) (or setHex, or setStyle for a CSS string). Pass color in the constructor options when creating.

lessons.title: A ShaderMaterial does no color space conversion unless you include it
lessons.symptom: A custom shader looks darker or with different colors than the built in materials next to it.
lessons.cause: The built in materials end with the tone mapping and color space chunks. A ShaderMaterial writes its color as is.
lessons.fix: End the fragment shader with the chunks tonemapping_fragment and colorspace_fragment (as include lines), or convert colors yourself.

lessons.title: PointLight and SpotLight use physical units since r155, so old intensities are far too dark
lessons.symptom: After an upgrade, or with code from an older tutorial, point and spot lights barely light anything.
lessons.cause: r155 made physical lighting the default: decay is 2 and intensity is in candela, so light falls off with the square of distance. The old useLegacyLights switch was deprecated then and removed later.
lessons.fix: Raise PointLight and SpotLight intensity a lot (tens to thousands, depending on distance), keep decay 2, and remove useLegacyLights. Tune with a slider while looking at the scene.

lessons.title: Metallic materials look black without an environment map
lessons.symptom: A chrome or gold model looks black or flat dark grey, even with bright lights.
lessons.cause: A fully metallic surface has no diffuse color; it only reflects its surroundings. Without scene.environment there is nothing to reflect but tiny light highlights.
lessons.fix: Set scene.environment to a PMREM of RoomEnvironment (pmrem.fromScene(new RoomEnvironment()).texture) or of an HDR loaded with HDRLoader.

lessons.title: RGBELoader was renamed HDRLoader in r180
lessons.symptom: The console warns that RGBELoader is deprecated, or an import of HDRLoader fails on an older three.
lessons.cause: r180 renamed the loader for .hdr files.
lessons.fix: Import HDRLoader from three/addons/loaders/HDRLoader.js on r180 and later; keep RGBELoader only for older versions.

lessons.title: A DirectionalLight points at its target, which must be in the scene to move
lessons.symptom: Moving light.target does not change the light direction, or the shadow does not follow the player.
lessons.cause: The light shines from its position toward target.position, using the target's world matrix. A target that is not in the scene never gets its matrix updated.
lessons.fix: Add light.target to the scene (or to the object it should follow) and move both the light and the target together.

lessons.title: No shadow draws until renderer.shadowMap.enabled is true
lessons.symptom: castShadow and receiveShadow are set, but there is no shadow.
lessons.cause: Shadows need three switches: the renderer's shadow map, castShadow on the light, and castShadow or receiveShadow on the meshes.
lessons.fix: Set renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true, light.castShadow = true, mesh.castShadow on casters and mesh.receiveShadow on the ground.

lessons.title: Set castShadow on each mesh of a loaded model, not on the root
lessons.symptom: A loaded model throws no shadow, although the ground receives shadows from other objects.
lessons.cause: castShadow is read per mesh; setting it on gltf.scene, a Group, does not reach the meshes inside.
lessons.fix: Traverse the model and set castShadow and receiveShadow on every child where isMesh is true.

lessons.title: A DirectionalLight casts shadows only inside its shadow camera box
lessons.symptom: Shadows are cut off, missing beyond a few units, or appear only near the center of the scene.
lessons.cause: The shadow camera of a DirectionalLight is orthographic, 10 units wide by default. Anything outside left, right, top, bottom, near and far gets no shadow.
lessons.fix: Set light.shadow.camera left, right, top, bottom, near and far to fit the area that needs shadows, call updateProjectionMatrix() on it, and check it with a CameraHelper.
lessons.test: Add a CameraHelper for light.shadow.camera and make sure the box covers the casters and the receivers.

lessons.title: Stripes on lit surfaces are shadow acne, fixed with bias
lessons.symptom: Moire stripes or dark bands on surfaces that face the light, or shadows that float off the ground.
lessons.cause: The surface shadows itself because of limited depth precision in the shadow map. Too much bias then detaches shadows from their casters.
lessons.fix: Set a small light.shadow.bias (about -0.0005) or a normalBias (0.02 to 0.05), and tighten the shadow camera so the precision goes where it is needed.

lessons.title: Blurry shadows come from a shadow camera that is too big, not from a small map
lessons.symptom: Shadows are soft and blocky, and raising mapSize to 8192 costs a lot of memory and speed.
lessons.cause: The shadow map is spread over the whole shadow camera box. A box far larger than the scene leaves few texels per unit.
lessons.fix: Shrink the shadow camera to the visible area (or move it with the player) before raising mapSize; 2048 is usually enough.

lessons.title: PCFSoftShadowMap is deprecated since r182; PCFShadowMap is soft now
lessons.symptom: The console warns about PCFSoftShadowMap and shadows look different after an upgrade.
lessons.cause: r182 deprecated PCFSoftShadowMap in WebGLRenderer and made PCFShadowMap soft; in r187 the renderer falls back to PCFShadowMap.
lessons.fix: Set renderer.shadowMap.type to THREE.PCFShadowMap and tune light.shadow.radius if needed.

lessons.title: Unexpected token '<' means the server sent an HTML page instead of the model
lessons.symptom: GLTFLoader or FileLoader fails with: Unexpected token '<', or a message that the response is not valid JSON.
lessons.cause: The URL is wrong. A dev server or an SPA host answers unknown paths with index.html, so the loader parses HTML.
lessons.fix: Open the model URL in the browser and fix the path until it downloads the file. Put static files in the folder the server serves (public in Vite).
lessons.test: Open the URL in a new tab, or read the content type in the network panel: it must not be text/html.

lessons.title: A Draco compressed glTF needs a DRACOLoader on the GLTFLoader
lessons.symptom: Loading fails with: No DRACOLoader instance provided.
lessons.cause: The file uses KHR_draco_mesh_compression, and GLTFLoader has no decoder of its own.
lessons.fix: Create a DRACOLoader, call setDecoderPath with a folder that holds the decoder files, and hand it to the GLTFLoader with setDRACOLoader.

lessons.title: Decoder files must be served from the path you give the loader
lessons.symptom: Draco or Basis loading hangs or fails with a WebAssembly error about a magic word or a MIME type.
lessons.cause: setDecoderPath or setTranscoderPath points to a folder the server does not have, so the browser gets an HTML page instead of the wasm file.
lessons.fix: Copy the files from three/examples/jsm/libs/draco/ (or libs/basis/) into the public folder and point the loader there, with a trailing slash. Serve wasm as application/wasm.
lessons.test: Open the decoder path plus draco_decoder.wasm in the browser: it must download a binary file.

lessons.title: KTX2 textures need a KTX2Loader that knows the renderer
lessons.symptom: A glTF with KTX2 textures fails to load, or a KTX2Loader throws about missing initialization.
lessons.cause: GLTFLoader needs a KTX2Loader for KHR_texture_basisu, and the KTX2Loader must know which compressed formats the GPU supports.
lessons.fix: Create a KTX2Loader, call setTranscoderPath and detectSupport(renderer), then hand it to the GLTFLoader with setKTX2Loader. With WebGPURenderer, await renderer.init() first; detectSupportAsync is deprecated since r181.
errors: setKTX2Loader must be called before loading KTX2 textures

lessons.title: A meshopt compressed glTF needs setMeshoptDecoder
lessons.symptom: Loading fails with setMeshoptDecoder must be called before loading compressed files.
lessons.cause: The file was compressed with gltfpack or gltf-transform using EXT_meshopt_compression.
lessons.fix: Import MeshoptDecoder from three/addons/libs/meshopt_decoder.module.js and pass it to setMeshoptDecoder on the GLTFLoader.
errors: setMeshoptDecoder must be called before loading compressed files

lessons.title: Open the page through a local server, not as a file
lessons.symptom: The page opened by double clicking index.html shows nothing; modules, models and textures are blocked.
lessons.cause: Browsers block ES modules and fetch for file URLs: the origin is null, so every request fails the CORS check.
lessons.fix: Serve the folder, for example with npx vite or npx serve, and open the localhost address it prints.
errors: Cross origin requests are only supported for protocol schemes

lessons.title: Textures from another domain need CORS headers
lessons.symptom: A texture from a CDN or an image host does not load, or WebGL refuses to upload it.
lessons.cause: WebGL may only use cross origin images when the server sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Without it the image is tainted.
lessons.fix: Host the image next to the page, or serve it with Access-Control-Allow-Origin and keep the loader crossOrigin at anonymous (the default).
errors: has been blocked by CORS policy

lessons.title: In Vite, files in public are served from the root, without public in the URL
lessons.symptom: A model or texture loads in one setup and gives a 404 or an unexpected token error in another.
lessons.cause: Vite serves the public folder at the site root, so a file in public/models is at /models. A path with public in it, or a path relative to the source file, does not exist on the server.
lessons.fix: Load files from public with a root URL such as /models/scene.glb, or import a file from src with the ?url suffix and pass that URL to the loader.

lessons.title: Root paths break when the site is deployed under a subpath
lessons.symptom: Everything works on localhost, but on GitHub Pages or another subpath host the models and textures give 404.
lessons.cause: The site lives under a subpath, while paths like /models/scene.glb point to the domain root. Vite's base option only rewrites paths it bundles.
lessons.fix: Set base in the Vite config to the subpath and build asset URLs from import.meta.env.BASE_URL, or use relative paths.

lessons.title: A model can only be used inside the load callback or after await
lessons.symptom: Cannot read properties of undefined when code touches the model right after calling load().
lessons.cause: Loaders are asynchronous. The variable is still undefined when the next line runs, and in the animation loop until loading finishes.
lessons.fix: Use await loader.loadAsync(url) in an async function, or do the work in the onLoad callback, and guard the loop until the model exists.

lessons.title: A texture put on a glTF mesh needs flipY false
lessons.symptom: A texture loaded with TextureLoader and assigned to a mesh from a glTF shows upside down or scrambled.
lessons.cause: glTF UVs have their origin at the top left, and GLTFLoader loads its own textures with flipY false. TextureLoader defaults to flipY true.
lessons.fix: Set texture.flipY = false (and colorSpace for color maps) before you assign it to a glTF material.

lessons.title: Convert FBX and OBJ to glTF for the web
lessons.symptom: An FBX model is 100 times too big, lies on its side, has shiny Phong materials or missing textures.
lessons.cause: FBX and OBJ have no fixed units, axes or PBR materials; their loaders guess. glTF is the format three supports best.
lessons.fix: Export glTF (.glb) from Blender, or convert with a tool such as gltf-transform, and load it with GLTFLoader.
errors: You are loading an asset with a Z-UP coordinate system

lessons.title: A glTF that references outside textures needs them next to it
lessons.symptom: The model loads but is white or grey, and the console says a texture could not be loaded.
lessons.cause: A .gltf file points to image files by relative path; they were not copied, were renamed, or the case of the name differs on a Linux server.
lessons.fix: Export a single .glb with the textures inside, or copy the images with the exact names the .gltf uses.

lessons.title: Add gltf.scene to the scene, not the gltf result
lessons.symptom: Nothing shows, and the console says the object is not an instance of THREE.Object3D.
lessons.cause: GLTFLoader returns an object with scene, scenes, animations and cameras. The result itself is not an Object3D.
lessons.fix: Call scene.add(gltf.scene).
errors: object not an instance of THREE.Object3D

lessons.title: Frame a model from its bounding box instead of guessing its size
lessons.symptom: The model loaded without errors but is invisible: far too small, far too big, or behind the camera.
lessons.cause: Models come in any unit (centimeters, meters, inches) and at any offset. A fixed camera position fits only one size.
lessons.fix: Compute new THREE.Box3().setFromObject(model), take its size and center, then scale the model or move the camera to a distance of about 1.5 times the largest side, and set near and far from that size. To fix a pivot that is off center, subtract the box center from model.position and move a parent Group instead.
lessons.test: Log the box size; a size of thousands or of 0.01 means the units are off.

lessons.title: An object has one parent: adding it twice moves it
lessons.symptom: Placing the same model in several spots shows only the last one.
lessons.cause: add() removes the object from its old parent first. One Object3D cannot be in two places.
lessons.fix: Use model.clone() for each copy (geometry and materials are shared), or an InstancedMesh for many copies of one mesh.

lessons.title: Clone a skinned character with SkeletonUtils.clone
lessons.symptom: Cloned characters stand in the bind pose, are stretched, or all move with the first one.
lessons.cause: Object3D.clone() copies the meshes but they stay bound to the bones of the original.
lessons.fix: Import clone from three/addons/utils/SkeletonUtils.js and clone with it; give each clone its own AnimationMixer.

lessons.title: Animated characters can vanish near the screen edge because of their bounding sphere
lessons.symptom: A skinned or morphing character pops out of view near the edges or while it moves far from its origin.
lessons.cause: Frustum culling uses a bounding sphere computed once. When animation moves the vertices away from that pose, the sphere no longer covers them.
lessons.fix: Call computeBoundingSphere() on the SkinnedMesh after the animation moves it, make the sphere larger, or set frustumCulled false on that mesh.

lessons.title: Meshes share materials, so changing one changes them all
lessons.symptom: Highlighting one selected object changes the color of other objects as well.
lessons.cause: Loaders and clone() reuse material objects between meshes.
lessons.fix: Clone the material before changing it on one mesh (mesh.material = mesh.material.clone()), and dispose the clone when done.

lessons.title: NaN in vertex positions breaks culling and picking
lessons.symptom: The mesh never shows or flickers, and the console says the computed radius is NaN.
lessons.cause: A position attribute holds NaN, usually from dividing by zero or from reading past the end of an array when building geometry.
lessons.fix: Check the numbers you write into the Float32Array, guard divisions, and recompute the bounding sphere after the fix.

lessons.title: GLTFLoader removes dots and spaces from node names
lessons.symptom: getObjectByName with the name from Blender returns undefined when the name has a dot or a space in it.
lessons.cause: Names are passed through PropertyBinding.sanitizeNodeName: spaces become underscores and the characters [ ] . : and slash are removed.
lessons.fix: Look the name up after sanitizing it the same way, or log the names with traverse to see what the loader made of them.

lessons.title: OrbitControls, GLTFLoader and other addons are not exported by three
lessons.symptom: The browser says the module three does not provide an export named OrbitControls, or THREE.OrbitControls is not a constructor.
lessons.cause: Controls, loaders, post processing and utils live in the addons, not in the core build.
lessons.fix: Import them from their file, such as three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js and three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js.

lessons.title: Without a bundler, the bare name three needs an import map
lessons.symptom: Failed to resolve module specifier three, and nothing runs.
lessons.cause: Browsers only load modules by URL. The bare specifier three means something only to a bundler, or through an import map.
lessons.fix: Add an importmap script before the module script that maps three to the build/three.module.js URL and three/addons/ to the examples/jsm/ URL, both at the same pinned version.

lessons.title: Import statements need a module script
lessons.symptom: Cannot use import statement outside a module.
lessons.cause: The script tag has no type module, or the file runs as CommonJS in Node or in a server render.
lessons.fix: Use a script tag with type module. In Node, set type module in package.json. In Next.js, add three to transpilePackages in the Next config.
errors: Cannot use import statement outside a module

lessons.title: The global THREE scripts from old tutorials were removed
lessons.symptom: THREE.OrbitControls is not a constructor, or the examples/js script returns 404, with code copied from an old answer.
lessons.cause: r148 removed the examples/js folder and r161 removed build/three.js and build/three.min.js. Only ES modules remain.
lessons.fix: Switch to ES modules: an import map (or a bundler), then import three and the addons from their module files.
errors: is not exported under the conditions

lessons.title: Addon imports need the .js extension
lessons.symptom: Node says it cannot find the addon module, although the file is there with a .js extension. Vite adds the extension itself, so the same path may work in the dev server.
lessons.cause: The exports map of three maps three/addons/* to files, so the path must name the file with its extension.
lessons.fix: Write three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js, not three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.

lessons.title: Two copies of three break instanceof checks and shared state
lessons.symptom: The console warns that multiple instances of Three.js are being imported; objects from a library do not render or controls do nothing.
lessons.cause: Two different copies of three are loaded: a CDN and npm mixed, a library that bundles its own three, or packages that need different versions.
lessons.fix: Run npm ls three and make it resolve once (npm dedupe, overrides in package.json, or resolve.dedupe in Vite). Load three from one place only.
lessons.test: npm ls three must show a single version, and the warning must be gone from the console.
errors: Multiple instances of Three.js being imported

lessons.title: Pin the three version in CDN URLs, and use the same one for the addons
lessons.symptom: A page that worked breaks one day, or addons fail because they are newer than the core.
lessons.cause: An unpinned CDN URL follows the latest release, and three changes its API between releases.
lessons.fix: Put an exact version in every URL (three@0.187.0), the same for three and three/addons/.

lessons.title: THREE.Geometry is gone since r125 and the BufferGeometry aliases since r144
lessons.symptom: Geometry is not a constructor, BoxBufferGeometry is not exported, or geometry.vertices is undefined.
lessons.cause: r125 removed Geometry and Face3 from the core; r144 deprecated the names ending in BufferGeometry (BoxBufferGeometry), which were removed later.
lessons.fix: Use BoxGeometry, PlaneGeometry and friends, and read or write vertices through geometry.attributes.position.

lessons.title: TextGeometry and FontLoader moved to the addons in r133
lessons.symptom: THREE.TextGeometry is not a constructor, or FontLoader is not exported by three.
lessons.cause: r133 moved TextGeometry and FontLoader out of the core.
lessons.fix: Import TextGeometry from three/addons/geometries/TextGeometry.js and FontLoader from three/addons/loaders/FontLoader.js; load a typeface JSON font.

lessons.title: three runs only in the browser; keep it out of server rendering
lessons.symptom: window is not defined, document is not defined or self is not defined during next build or a server render.
lessons.cause: Next.js, Nuxt and others run components on the server first, where there is no DOM, canvas or WebGL.
lessons.fix: Mark the component as a client component and load the 3D view with next/dynamic with ssr set to false (or a client only wrapper); create the renderer in an effect, not at import time.

lessons.title: Cap the pixel ratio at 2
lessons.symptom: Low frame rate and hot phones on high density screens, while the scene is simple.
lessons.cause: setPixelRatio(window.devicePixelRatio) renders 9 to 16 times the pixels on screens with a ratio of 3 or 4.
lessons.fix: Use renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2)).

lessons.title: Use InstancedMesh for many copies of one mesh
lessons.symptom: A forest, a crowd or a particle field of separate meshes runs slowly; renderer.info.render.calls is in the thousands.
lessons.cause: Every Mesh is its own draw call with its own matrix update.
lessons.fix: Draw the copies with one InstancedMesh and setMatrixAt, or merge static meshes with mergeGeometries from BufferGeometryUtils. BatchedMesh fits different shapes that share a material.
lessons.test: Read renderer.info.render.calls before and after; it should drop to a handful.

lessons.title: After setMatrixAt, flag instanceMatrix and recompute the bounding sphere
lessons.symptom: Instances do not move, or all instances vanish when the camera turns.
lessons.cause: setMatrixAt writes into the array only; the GPU copy updates when instanceMatrix.needsUpdate is true. Since r151 InstancedMesh is frustum culled with a bounding sphere computed once, which no longer fits moved instances.
lessons.fix: Set mesh.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true (and instanceColor.needsUpdate after setColorAt), then call mesh.computeBoundingSphere() when instances moved, or set frustumCulled false for fields that move every frame.

lessons.title: Edited BufferAttributes need needsUpdate, and they cannot grow
lessons.symptom: Changing vertex positions does nothing, or new points beyond the first count never appear.
lessons.cause: The GPU buffer is uploaded once. Changes need attribute.needsUpdate = true, and a buffer keeps its first size.
lessons.fix: Set needsUpdate after each edit. Allocate the largest size up front and show part of it with geometry.setDrawRange, or dispose the geometry and create a new one. Recompute bounding volumes when the shape changes.
errors: Buffer size too small for points data

lessons.title: Do not create vectors or matrices every frame
lessons.symptom: Regular small stutters, and the memory graph saw-tooths in the performance panel.
lessons.cause: new Vector3() and friends in the loop create garbage that the browser has to collect.
lessons.fix: Create the helper objects once outside the loop and reuse them with set(), copy() and the target arguments of methods such as getWorldPosition(target).

lessons.title: Never create geometries, materials or loaders in the render loop
lessons.symptom: The frame rate falls over time and GPU memory keeps rising.
lessons.cause: Each new geometry or material allocates GPU memory and can compile a new shader; nothing disposes the old ones.
lessons.fix: Create them once and change their properties or uniforms in the loop.

lessons.title: Compile shaders before a new material first shows
lessons.symptom: The scene freezes for a moment the first time an object, a light or an effect appears.
lessons.cause: The shader program is built on first use. Adding a light or turning on shadows changes the programs of every lit material.
lessons.fix: Keep the number of lights fixed, and call renderer.compileAsync(scene, camera) while loading so the programs are ready before they are needed.

lessons.title: Removing an object from the scene does not free GPU memory
lessons.symptom: Memory and renderer.info.memory counts grow each time objects are replaced, until the tab slows or crashes.
lessons.cause: Geometries, materials, textures and render targets keep their GPU buffers until dispose() is called.
lessons.fix: When an object is gone for good, call dispose() on its geometry, its materials, every texture map of those materials (material.dispose() leaves them) and any render target.
lessons.test: Log renderer.info.memory before and after replacing the objects a few times; the counts must not keep rising.

lessons.title: Tear down the renderer when a view goes away
lessons.symptom: Each visit to the 3D page in a single page app adds memory, more event listeners and finally a lost context.
lessons.cause: The animation loop, event listeners, controls and the renderer stay alive after the component is gone.
lessons.fix: On unmount: renderer.setAnimationLoop(null), controls.dispose(), remove your listeners, dispose the scene contents, renderer.dispose(), and remove the canvas.

lessons.title: Compute mouse coordinates from the canvas rectangle, not the window
lessons.symptom: Clicking picks the wrong object or nothing, and the offset grows away from the top left.
lessons.cause: Normalized device coordinates must be relative to the canvas. Using the window size is wrong as soon as the canvas is not full screen or the page scrolls.
lessons.fix: Take rect = renderer.domElement.getBoundingClientRect(), then x = ((event.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * 2 - 1 and y = -((event.clientY - rect.top) / rect.height) * 2 + 1.

lessons.title: A raycast hit is the inner mesh, not the model you added
lessons.symptom: Clicking a loaded model returns a mesh you never named, and its userData is empty.
lessons.cause: intersectObjects returns the deepest meshes that were hit; the Group you added is a parent of them.
lessons.fix: Walk up hit.object.parent until you reach the object you tagged (in userData), or raycast against a short list of the objects you care about.

lessons.title: OrbitControls turns around controls.target, not around the model
lessons.symptom: The camera orbits around an empty point and the model swings out of view.
lessons.cause: The target defaults to the origin, and camera.lookAt is overwritten by the controls.
lessons.fix: Set controls.target to the model center and call controls.update(); do not call camera.lookAt while controls are active.

lessons.title: Damping needs controls.update() every frame
lessons.symptom: With enableDamping on, the camera stops dead, or moves only on the next interaction.
lessons.cause: Damping is applied in update(), so it must run in the loop.
lessons.fix: Call controls.update() in the animation loop.

lessons.title: Controls need the canvas element to listen to
lessons.symptom: OrbitControls exist but dragging does nothing, or keys do nothing.
lessons.cause: Without renderer.domElement as the second argument the controls have nowhere to listen. Since r124 OrbitControls listen to keys only after listenToKeyEvents.
lessons.fix: Create them with new OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement), and call controls.listenToKeyEvents(window) for arrow keys.

lessons.title: An AnimationMixer moves nothing unless update runs every frame
lessons.symptom: The glTF animation never plays; the character stays in its rest pose.
lessons.cause: action.play() only marks the action as active. The mixer moves time forward only in mixer.update(delta).
lessons.fix: Create the mixer on gltf.scene, play an action from gltf.animations, and call mixer.update(delta) in the loop with the time since the last frame.

lessons.title: Move by delta time, not by a fixed step per frame
lessons.symptom: Things move twice as fast on a 120 Hz screen, and slow down when the frame rate drops.
lessons.cause: A fixed increment per frame ties speed to the refresh rate.
lessons.fix: Multiply speeds by the delta from a Timer (timer.update() then timer.getDelta()) and clamp large deltas after the tab was hidden.

lessons.title: getElapsedTime() resets the delta of the same Clock
lessons.symptom: mixer.update(clock.getDelta()) plays nothing or very slowly, while elapsed time looks fine.
lessons.cause: Clock.getElapsedTime calls getDelta inside, so a second call in the same frame returns almost 0.
lessons.fix: Read the delta once per frame and add it up yourself, or use THREE.Timer (Clock is deprecated since r183).

lessons.title: WebGPURenderer has to finish init before the first render
lessons.symptom: An error says render() was called before the backend is initialized.
lessons.cause: WebGPURenderer starts asynchronously. render(), clear() and PMREMGenerator calls before that throw.
lessons.fix: await renderer.init() before rendering, or start drawing with renderer.setAnimationLoop, which waits for init.
errors: called before the backend is initialized

lessons.title: Import WebGPURenderer from three/webgpu and TSL from three/tsl
lessons.symptom: three does not export WebGPURenderer, or node materials and TSL functions are missing.
lessons.cause: Since r171 the WebGPU renderer, the node materials and TSL are built into separate entries: three/webgpu and three/tsl.
lessons.fix: Import everything for a WebGPU app from three/webgpu (it also holds the core classes) and TSL from three/tsl; with an import map, map both.

lessons.title: ShaderMaterial and onBeforeCompile do not work with WebGPURenderer
lessons.symptom: A custom GLSL material shows nothing or errors under WebGPURenderer.
lessons.cause: WebGPURenderer builds shaders from node materials. GLSL strings and onBeforeCompile hooks are WebGL only.
lessons.fix: Port the shader to TSL with a node material (colorNode, positionNode), or stay on WebGLRenderer for that material.

lessons.title: EffectComposer is for WebGLRenderer; WebGPU uses RenderPipeline
lessons.symptom: Post processing passes do nothing or fail with WebGPURenderer.
lessons.cause: EffectComposer and its passes are built on WebGL render targets and GLSL. WebGPU has its own pipeline; PostProcessing was renamed RenderPipeline in r183.
lessons.fix: Use RenderPipeline from three/webgpu with pass() and the effect nodes from three/addons/tsl/, or keep WebGLRenderer when you need EffectComposer.

lessons.title: WebGPURenderer falls back to WebGL 2 where WebGPU is missing
lessons.symptom: Features differ between browsers, or code that checks for WebGPU fails on Safari or Linux.
lessons.cause: When navigator.gpu is missing, WebGPURenderer uses its WebGL 2 backend. Some features (compute shaders, some texture formats) are limited there.
lessons.fix: Test with both backends (forceWebGL true in the options), and read renderer.backend.isWebGPUBackend before using WebGPU only features.

lessons.title: useFrame and useThree work only inside the Canvas
lessons.symptom: R3F says hooks can only be used within the Canvas component.
lessons.cause: These hooks read the R3F store that the Canvas creates. A component that uses them but renders outside the Canvas has no store.
lessons.fix: Move the component (or the hook) into a child of the Canvas, and pass data out through a state store or callbacks.
errors: Hooks can only be used within the Canvas component

lessons.title: HTML elements cannot go inside the Canvas
lessons.symptom: R3F says Div is not part of the THREE namespace.
lessons.cause: Everything inside the Canvas is turned into three objects; a div or a button has no three class. The same message shows for a removed class such as BoxBufferGeometry.
lessons.fix: Put HTML outside the Canvas in a positioned overlay, or use the Html component of drei to place it in the scene. Rename removed classes (boxGeometry).
errors: is not part of the THREE namespace

lessons.title: Match the R3F major version to React: fiber 8 with React 18, fiber 9 with React 19
lessons.symptom: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading ReactCurrentOwner) on start, often in a new Next.js 15 project.
lessons.cause: R3F 8 uses React 18 internals that React 19 removed.
lessons.fix: With React 19 install fiber 9 and drei 10; with React 18 keep fiber 8 and drei 9. Check with npm ls react.

lessons.title: Do not set React state in useFrame; change the object through a ref
lessons.symptom: The scene stutters and React re-renders the component every frame.
lessons.cause: useFrame runs 60 or more times per second. A state update there re-renders the component tree each time.
lessons.fix: Keep a ref to the mesh and change ref.current.position or rotation directly in useFrame. Keep state for changes that the UI shows.

lessons.title: Objects created in the component body are rebuilt on every render
lessons.symptom: GPU memory grows and the scene hitches whenever the component re-renders.
lessons.cause: new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial() or a geometry made in the function body is a new object on each render, and the old one is never disposed.
lessons.fix: Declare geometry and materials as JSX children, or create them with useMemo; for loaded data use the loader hooks, which cache.

lessons.title: Wrap loading components in Suspense inside the Canvas
lessons.symptom: The whole canvas stays empty until everything loads, or React complains that a component suspended.
lessons.cause: useLoader and useGLTF suspend until the file is loaded. Without a Suspense boundary close to them, React suspends a larger part of the tree.
lessons.fix: Put a Suspense with a fallback around each loading part, inside the Canvas, so the rest of the scene renders right away.
errors: A component suspended while responding to synchronous input

lessons.title: useGLTF returns the same scene for the same URL, so clone it for each copy
lessons.symptom: Rendering a model component twice shows the model only once.
lessons.cause: useGLTF caches by URL, so every component gets the same Object3D, and an object can have only one parent.
lessons.fix: Use the Clone component of drei, or scene.clone() in useMemo (SkeletonUtils clone for skinned models).

lessons.title: The R3F Canvas turns on ACES tone mapping and sRGB output by default
lessons.symptom: Colors in an R3F scene look different from the same code in plain three, or from the design.
lessons.cause: R3F sets ACESFilmicToneMapping on the renderer unless told otherwise.
lessons.fix: Add the flat prop to the Canvas for NoToneMapping, or set toneMapped false on single materials; set the tone mapping you want through the gl prop.

lessons.title: With frameloop demand, call invalidate after a change
lessons.symptom: Changing a prop or an object in a handler has no effect until the mouse moves the controls.
lessons.cause: In demand mode R3F renders only when it knows something changed; a direct change through a ref does not tell it.
lessons.fix: Call invalidate() from useThree after changing objects directly.

lessons.title: A shader compile error names the line in the generated source
lessons.symptom: The material is invisible or the screen is black, and the console shows a shader error with a long listing.
lessons.cause: three adds its own lines before your GLSL, so the line number points into the full program. Common slips: a float written as 1 instead of 1.0, a missing semicolon, or texture2D in GLSL 3.
lessons.fix: Read the line marked in the listing, compare it with your shader, and write floats with a decimal point. Run threesmith explain on the message to map it back to your file.

lessons.title: Uniforms are objects with a value field, and you change the value
lessons.symptom: A uniform such as time never changes in the shader, or the material throws while rendering.
lessons.cause: ShaderMaterial expects each uniform as an object holding value. Replacing the whole uniform object, or passing a bare number, breaks the link to the program.
lessons.fix: Declare uTime with a value of 0 and update material.uniforms.uTime.value each frame.

lessons.title: A green build does not mean the scene renders
lessons.symptom: The code compiles and the tests pass, but the page shows a black canvas.
lessons.cause: Most three.js failures happen at runtime: lights, colors, camera, paths and shaders only show in a browser.
lessons.fix: Run threesmith check (or open the page) and look at the console messages and the screenshot before calling the work done.

lessons.title: Check names against the installed three, not against memory
lessons.symptom: Generated code uses classes, options or paths that no longer exist, or that never existed.
lessons.cause: three changes its API in many releases, and examples on the web span ten years of versions.
lessons.fix: Look names up with threesmith api for the installed version, and run threesmith review to catch removed and renamed APIs.
